title: Nilo-Saharan languages - Wikipedia
text: The Nilo-Saharan languages are a proposed linguistic family consisting of around 210 Native African languages spoken by somewhere around 70 million speakers, mainly in the upper parts of the Chari and Nile rivers, including historic Nubia, north of where the two tributaries of the Nile meet.

title: Runga - grokipedia.com
text: The Runga are part of the Sudanic peoples, historically shaped by Arab influences—evident in the exonym "Runga" bestowed by Chadian Arabs—and have been involved in regional conflicts, such as in the Central African Republic where local Runga groups formed militias in response to violence with nomadic herdsmen from Chad and Sudan.
